page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Running head at the top, centred, with the page number at the top right. No marginal notes and no footnotes. No catchword or signature.

main_text.p: mare rubrum, & transit in regiones Æthiopum, secatq; Nilum Ægypti: in regno Æthiopum insignes civitates sunt Huma, Dyntala, & multæ aliæ. Hoc idem clima postremo tendit ad occidentem, & per meridionales regiones Barbarorum transit, donec perveniat ad mare occidentale.

Secundum clima incipit ab oriente, & transit per regiones Sin & Indiæ, qua parte civitates sunt Almansoria, Aliabran & Adubil: deinde vadit per combinationes maris viridis & Albasara, & secat infulam Arabum, circa terram Nagoni & Tuema: ubi celebres civitates sunt Aliomenlach[?], Albarahen, Hogor, Vetabh, Alior, Mecha, Acajis & Geda: postea secat mare rubrum, & transit per Sajir Ægypti, secatq; Nilum, qua parte civitates sunt Cabrus, Hacuim, Hansche[?], Astar[?], Azsahe, Afin & Esron: deinde pervenit versus occidentem in regnum Africæ, & transit regiones Barbarorum, donec attingat mare occidentale.

Tertium clima incipit ab oriente, & transit partem septentrionalem regni Sin: deinde pergit ad regiones Kebil, Carmen, Seruasten, & Alexandriam Muhamedanam, Ebroab & Asoceran: postea transit per littora maris Albasara, ubi civitates sunt Astachar, Iothor, Fefe, Sabor, Secren, Siref, Kalbone, Senemir & Maruben: & vadit per diœceses Alguez & Algrath, ubi urbes sunt Albasa, Guaisit, Baged, Ascua, Alenbei, & Sond: postea

page.notes: Running head read as CAPVT XI. and given as CAPUT XI. because the V is a vowel here. The page number is printed as a figure with a glyph that looks like long s; read as 45. Doubtful readings marked [?]: Aliomenlach (a mark stands over the initial A), Hansche, and Astar (both have marks over them). Several place names carry small diacritic marks over the initial letter that could not be read with certainty. Printed spelling kept, including "Afin", "Sajir", "Asoceran", and "Seruasten".
